definitions.gloss: absent-mindedly; spaced out; in a daze
definitions.explanation: Describes being mentally unfocused, zoning out, or not paying attention.
Describes something appearing unclear or indistinct.

examples.english: I'm so tired I can't focus.

examples.japanese: {授業|じゅぎょう}{中|ちゅう}にぼーっとしていた。
examples.english: I was spaced out during class.

examples.japanese: ぼーっと{窓|まど}の{外|そと}を{見|み}ていた。
examples.english: I was staring absently out the window.

examples.japanese: {風邪|かぜ}をひいて{頭|あたま}がぼーっとする。
examples.english: I have a cold and my head feels foggy.

examples.japanese: {遠|とお}くの{景色|けしき}がぼーっと{見|み}える。
{霧|きり}でぼーっとしか{見|み}えない。
examples.english: I can only see hazily because of the fog.

examples.japanese: {明|あ}かりがぼーっと{光|ひか}っている。
{暗|くら}い{中|なか}にぼーっと{人影|ひとかげ}が{見|み}えた。
examples.english: I could vaguely see a figure in the darkness.

examples.japanese: {眼鏡|めがね}を{外|はず}すと{全部|ぜんぶ}ぼーっと{見|み}える。
examples.english: When I take off my glasses, everything looks blurry.

notes:
ぼーっと is an onomatopoeic word describing mental or visual haziness. The two senses are related: both convey a lack of sharpness or focus.

Sense 1 (mental): Describes being spaced out, absent-minded, or unable to concentrate. ぼーっとする is extremely common in daily conversation.

Sense 2 (visual): Describes something appearing blurry, hazy, or indistinct — like shapes in fog or dim light.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ぼーっとする: to space out, zone out
- ぼーっと{見|み}る: to stare blankly
- ぼーっと{過|す}ごす: to spend time idly
- {頭|あたま}がぼーっとする: head feels foggy

TYPICAL CAUSES:
- {疲|つか}れ (tiredness)
- {寝不足|ねぶそく} (lack of sleep)
- {風邪|かぜ} (cold/illness)
- {考|かんが}え{事|ごと} (lost in thought)

Note: ぼーっとするな is a common scolding expression meaning "Pay attention!" or "Stop daydreaming!"
